newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-AGASSI, LEACH AND STARK NAMED TO U.S. DAVIS CUP TEAM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AGASSI, LEACH AND STARK NAMED TO U.S. DAVIS CUP TEAM.

text.p: Andre Agassi, Jonathan Stark and Rick Leach will join Jim Courier on the U.S. Davis Cup squad that will play the Netherlands in the quarter-finals next month, U.S. captain Tom Gullikson announced Wednesday.
Gullikson had named Courier to the team late last month, but held off selecting the rest of the squad due to the uncertain status of several top American players.

The 13th-ranked Agassi has struggled to find his form of late but takes a 22-4 singles record and a 13-match Davis Cup winning streak into the April 4-6 quarter-finals on hard court at the Palisades Tennis Club in Newport Beach, California.
Agassi last played Davis Cup in the 1995 semifinal victory over Sweden and was a member of the U.S. Davis Cup-winning teams in 1990 and 1992.
"These three players, along with Jim Courier, all have Davis Cup experience," Gullikson said in a statement issued by the United States Tennis Association.
"Agassi and Courier give us outstanding singles firepower, and Leach and Stark are a force in doubles," Gullikson said.
Leach, 7-1 in Davis Cup doubles, also was a member of the Cup-winning team in 1990 with former partner Jim Pugh.
Stark and Leach, the world's fifth-ranked doubles team, reached the Australian Open semifinals this year.
Courier, a member of Cup-winning teams in 1992 and 1995, won both his singles matches in the opening round against Brazil this year to raise his Davis Cup record to 11-7.
World number one Pete Sampras and third-ranked Michael Chang had indicated that they were not interested in playing Davis Cup until the later rounds.
And recent injuries to Agassi, Todd Martin and MaliVai Washington had forced Gullikson to hold off on naming his full team until Wednesday.
